research_updates.title: Parcel and appeal records connect the SV1 development to RagingWire
research_updates.notes: Santa Clara's development record identifies the SV1 project at 1150 Walsh Avenue on APN 224-58-003, while NTT's current facility page uses 1160 Walsh Avenue. The county appeal report names RagingWire Data Centers Inc. on that APN. These records support the project-to-parcel link, but no address-renumbering instrument was located, so both official address forms remain disclosed. County appeal positions are not final tax bills or payments; employment and water figures remain pre-opening forecasts.

economic_scope_note: Reviewed evidence batches at campus or company/county scope. No record is allocated to an individual inventory building. Source checking establishes what a document reports, not an independent audit or causal attribution. Monetary figures are nominal. Peak workforce is distinct from annual employment; source-year labels do not establish fiscal-year boundaries. Original forecasts remain forecasts until realization is verified. No cross-record benefit total is defined. Cumulative project costs are not annual expenditure. Tax receipts and incentive payments remain separate, with inferred taxpayer links disclosed. Contextual research updates do not count as economic amounts. Account tax bills are distinct from cash receipts and incentive-program fees. Tax years, calendar years and fiscal years retain their source basis; separate taxpayer accounts are not consolidated. Municipal developer rebates and taxpayer valuations have distinct subjects. Estimated actual property value and tax capacity are not tax receipts; payable-year valuations retain their earlier assessment date. Taxpayer values expressed in millions retain approximate precision and account-level separation. A current-year table can use an older valuation date and is not converted into an annual series. Facility real-property and business-personal-property accounts remain separate, and address-label discrepancies are disclosed. Michigan Industrial Facilities Tax accounts remain distinct from the underlying real parcel and from post-expiration personal-property accounts; annual account totals are not recipient-level government receipts. Permit construction values are administrative project amounts, not verified expenditure, and separate permits are not combined without proof that their scopes do not overlap. Repeated maintenance-year assessments are annual parcel stocks, not new investment flows. Mixed-use parcel assessments and taxable values are retained at whole-parcel scope and are not allocated to a data-center tenant or function by floor area. Operator-reported jobs supported remain distinct from direct employees and FTEs. Approved infrastructure grants are documented public commitments rather than verified disbursements or total public costs. Cumulative community funding remains separate from tax receipts, payroll and modeled multiplier effects. Reported facility power capacity is not measured electricity consumption or peak demand. Permit-listed emergency generators are not runtime, fuel-use or actual-emissions observations. A city largest-taxpayer table's personal-property assessment remains separate from the leasehold real-property account, tax bills, receipts and capital expenditure. TIF loan principal is financing rather than a grant or general-fund receipt; project-generated tax revenue pledged to repayment is retained as a separate public-financing flow and is not added to gross parcel distributions. Water-withdrawal and consumptive permit capacities are regulatory limits rather than measured use. Development-agreement local-labor preferences are requirements rather than realized participation, and operating employee snapshots remain distinct from customers' on-site staff and jobs forecasts. Audited City bond statements distinguish issuance draws, year-end principal, annual principal retired, interest and fees, pledged TIF revenue, debt-service-fund transfers and future principal-plus-interest commitments. These measures are not summed into a benefit or subsidy total. City pledged revenue, City debt-service-fund transfers and the private fund's project TIF revenue applied to loan repayment retain their separate source definitions because only the 2022 transfer and private-fund amount agree exactly. Developer testimony in public meeting minutes is retained as a source-attributed cumulative lower bound; local-contractor spending is not converted into payroll, worker counts, household spending or multiplier effects. Economic-improvement-district cost estimates and maximum owner assessments remain source projections until bond issuance, an assessment schedule, collections and expenditures are verified. A statutory financing cap is not a tax receipt, public expenditure or subsidy. Audited private equipment-financing balances are debt stocks rather than construction spending, public support or community benefit. Reported floor area and occupied-share values describe operating scale and utilization, not employment, revenue, power use or economic output. Contractor and engineer case studies document supplier roles and completion timing but do not establish payment amounts, worker residence, payroll or multiplier effects. State incentive contract amounts, expected jobs and paid-or-certified-to-date fields remain distinct; a zero paid/certified balance at an earlier reporting cutoff does not imply no later claims. Public charging-infrastructure awards are commitments rather than verified disbursements, private project investment or operating benefits. Qualitative payment descriptions without a defensible numeric bound remain research context rather than quantitative records. Program-reported actual qualified investment, certified tax-exemption value and certified tax-credit value remain separate cumulative measures; none is converted into annual spending, a cash grant, local revenue or causal impact. County Business Patterns observations are county-industry context, not project contributions: establishment counts are employer locations rather than data-center facilities, March employment is not an annual average, annual payroll spans the full NAICS cell, and disclosure noise, classification changes and geographic assignment limit comparisons. No CBP change is attributed to a study project. Project fragments: prj_study_im3_building_00364289074: Corrective public-source audit for Microsoft's data-center property at 5150 Rogers Road and explicitly labeled wider Microsoft/Bexar County activity. Exact-site ordinance, permit, appraisal, and tax-account records remain separate from later campuses and regional disclosures; the three appraisal accounts and two taxable-account payments are not consolidated. Permit value is administrative, the original investment and employment figures are commitments, the 2013 employment threshold is a reported lower bound, and the water quantity is a projection rather than metered consumption. No Bexar-and-Medina total is allocated to this property. Annual construction expenditure, construction labor and residence, supplier payments, operating payroll and purchases, recipient-level tax distributions, marginal public-service cost, electricity consumption, water withdrawal or consumption, wastewater, actual emissions, and a recurring facility-level community series remain unobserved after the documented searches. prj_study_im3_building_00377585075: Corrective DET01 evidence audit. Official parcel, permit, tax, water-account, state-certificate, EPA and operator records are retained as direct observations or clearly labeled source forecasts. Conflicting floor-area figures remain separate because their reporting definitions differ. Construction cost, realized jobs, supplier payments, community funding, electricity, emissions, wastewater, actual public-service cost and causal county effects remain unbounded rather than being filled with transferred assumptions. prj_study_im3_building_00460089167: Corrective primary-source audit adds current Andale parcel assessment, contractor-reported campus floor area, and two recipient- or government-reported Meta community grants. The search trail records useful and negative results across identity, tax, construction, jobs, suppliers, utilities, water, permits, public costs, incentives, community funding, and county comparison inputs. Campus-wide facts remain unallocated to the selected inventory building, overlapping community amounts are not added together, and unavailable supplier, payroll, utility-billing, discharge, generator, and marginal-service-cost amounts remain explicit gaps. prj_study_im3_building_00464097467: Second-pass public-evidence audit for Apple's Washoe County data-center campus at 21505 Reno Technology Parkway West and its 2024 expansion application. GOED audit findings, application forecasts, county permit values, parcel assessments, a water-right allocation, operator-reported electricity use, and recipient-reported donation bands remain separate evidence states and scopes. Permit values are administrative amounts and are not summed because overlapping scopes cannot be ruled out. Assessment values are parcel stocks, not investment or tax receipts. The 125 acre-foot water right is regulatory capacity, not measured use. Food Bank gifts are company-region transfers, not campus-attributable annual spending. No campus total is allocated to the selected mapped building; the four-building campus, later buildout cases, downtown Reno warehouse, supporting renewable projects, fire-station parcel, and more-than-200-person support statement are not collapsed into one footprint. No Switch Citadel or Storey County amount enters this fragment. Vendor payments, worker residence, taxes received by jurisdiction, realized 2024 abatement, same-scope public-service cost, wastewater, and building-level electricity or water remain unobserved. prj_study_im3_building_00664938835: Second-pass public-evidence audit for Expedient's adaptive reuse of the pre-existing data-center building at 4777 W Ironwood Drive. The review searched Franklin planning, agenda, assessment, permit, water and sewer materials; Milwaukee County tax and deed-record access points; Wisconsin DOR, WEDC, DFI and PSC records; operator press, specification, career, ESG and community pages; lease, financing, carrier and vendor disclosures; and archived official pages for 2007-2026. Opening-day and current operator specifications remain separate dated snapshots because the reported area and capacity changed. The county portal now establishes a 2021-2025 parcel-tax principal series, but not Expedient's incidence under the lease. The 2022 ownership transfer, assessments, estimated permit values, tax payments and hiring plan remain non-additive. No source was found for actual construction outlays, realized site employment or payroll, local procurement, Milwaukee-area community transfers, metered resources, project-attributable public costs or a fiscal net. prj_study_im3_building_01073720208: Second-pass public-evidence audit for Google's Council Bluffs data-center activity, retaining the selected inventory building as the project key while leaving campus, taxpayer-account, company-county, and state-award facts at their reported scopes. The audit distinguishes completed IEDA contracts 08-HQJC-030 and 12-HQJP-051 from the 2022 award still in performance; permit valuations remain administrative amounts rather than expenditure; assessed and taxable values remain stocks; bills remain distinct from payments; and community grants remain recipient- and period-specific. The Pottawattamie County tax portal now supplies a paid 2018-2024 series for the principal Tetra parcel and an unpaid 2025 bill for the newer Questa parcel. No value is inferred for sales-tax exemptions, the local abatement schedule, franchise-fee adjustment, electricity, supplier retention, building-level water, marginal public-service cost, or net fiscal position. Models without defensible project allocation or transferable parameters were removed even though that leaves the eight-category account incomplete.
modeled_scope_note: Modeled contribution accounts for Apple Mesa / Maricopa County, Switch Citadel / Storey County, and Digital Crossroad Hammond / Lake County. Every required account category and county-comparison module contains sourced evidence or a visibly labeled modeled value. Public support is not netted against unmatched local revenues, unavailable public-service cost is represented by a break-even threshold rather than an invented net margin, county comparisons are descriptive rather than causal, and low-confidence transferred benchmarks remain explicit. Project fragments: prj_study_im3_building_00364289074: Corrective residual modeled account for Microsoft San Antonio. Eight transferred construction, labor, procurement, operating, and household-output scenarios were removed because their arbitrary capital shares, forecast-realization cases, local-purchase assumptions, and Virginia coefficients were not bounded by project observations. Only three low-confidence descriptive county comparisons remain: each uses the project's documented operating-by 2013 anchor and official Bexar County outcome data, has a finite fit-sensitivity envelope, and explicitly makes no causal attribution. The account intentionally remains incomplete because no defensible direct observation or residual model closes the supplier category. prj_study_im3_building_00377585075: Corrective DET01 synthesis. Only exact same-period tax-account arithmetic, its explicitly conditional public-cost break-even identity and a unit conversion of displayed municipal meter history remain. Construction, employment, supplier, household, electricity, cooling, emissions, wastewater and county-effect models were removed because the audit did not bound the missing project inputs. This account is intentionally incomplete where direct evidence remains unbounded. prj_study_im3_building_00460089167: Corrective audit retains six bounded residual calculations only: FY2025 county tax retained after the provisionally linked incentive, the identical marginal-service-cost break-even threshold, conversion of Meta-reported 2024 water withdrawal with source rounding, and three noncausal county comparison gaps with fit sensitivity. Ten models based on arbitrary capital timing, cost shares, FTE ratios, transferred operating/construction multipliers, fleet PUE, or wastewater ratios are removed. Supplier/local-procurement evidence remains unavailable, so the project is intentionally incomplete rather than backfilled. prj_study_im3_building_00464097467: Second-pass modeled contribution account after an expanded public-evidence audit. Direct county permits now cover historical construction values, assessor rolls cover a main-campus parcel stock, a county action covers water-right capacity, Apple reports 2025 campus electricity use, and recipient reports bound two community gifts. Those observations supersede the need for a modeled community proxy but do not supply Apple contractor job-years, construction payroll, annual operating payroll, supplier payments, taxes received, or public-service cost. The construction base therefore retains only the packet's explicit $163 million construction forecast and excludes equipment and historical capital; wide 0.5-1.5 transfer sensitivities expose the mismatch in the last-resort direct construction coefficients. The unsupported local-purchase-share and Virginia induced-output models are removed. No net-fiscal value or public-service-cost break-even is published. County outcome gaps remain descriptive benchmark applications with fit-sensitivity intervals and no causal-design metadata. prj_study_im3_building_00664938835: Second-pass Expedient Milwaukee / Franklin syntheses retained only after a documented 2007-2026 public-source audit. The account keeps a clearly labeled 2022 ownership-transfer anchor, a PB25-0303-only construction allocation sensitivity, an exact tax-equal public-cost break-even threshold, a capacity-based electricity engineering sensitivity, and three descriptive county comparison gaps. It removes transferred construction job-years, assumed local-purchase shares, supplier and household output extrapolations, and a duplicate modeled tax row because public sources did not establish realized site employment, supplier geography, household capture, or a need to restate the direct tax observations. PM25-0174 remains excluded for possible overlap. No synthesis is an observed result or fiscal net. prj_study_im3_building_01073720208: Second-pass governed synthesis for Google Council Bluffs. Construction job-years use only two directly observed September 2025 city permit valuations and transfer the published Prince William County prototype coefficients as benchmark equivalents; the four channels are separated and protected by one aggregation. No Pottawattamie County supplier-retention share is imposed because the public audit found contractor names but no payment or vendor-residence ledger. The water row is the unallocated Google Council Bluffs location identity reported for 2024, not a building allocation. No local abatement, exemption realization, franchise-fee amount, electric load, public-service cost, break-even threshold, or net fiscal result is modeled. County outcome gaps remain descriptive benchmark applications with fit-sensitivity ranges and no causal attribution.
legacy_first_entry_note: Equinix SV1 was operational in Santa Clara County more than twenty-one years before NTT SV1 opened. The NTT event is therefore rejected as the county's first operational entry. The broader 74-facility historical inventory has not been proven complete, so the county's true first entry remains unresolved and no treatment date is assigned.
